title: Black Light FTL Route Segment Certification Registry

segmentPolicy.physicalEnvelope: Use the more severe endpoint value independently for each physical metric; never dimensionally average unlike metrics.
segmentPolicy.gradientDiagnostics: Use finite differences across the segment only as local engineering diagnostics, not analytic derivative proofs.
segmentPolicy.uncertaintyRule: Missing uncertainty remains unresolved. Segment certification may not substitute zero covariance or perfect ephemerides.
segmentPolicy.invalidModelRule: If either endpoint is OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY, the segment is OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY and blocks the route.
segmentPolicy.unresolvedRule: If either endpoint is UNRESOLVED, the segment is UNRESOLVED and blocks route certification.
segmentPolicy.partialRule: PARTIAL physical evidence is retained as unresolved certification evidence unless a higher-fidelity packet closes the missing fields.

potentialGradientAlongPathS2.note: Directional finite-difference potential gradient along the sampled route chord; it is not a replacement for the full acceleration vector.

accelerationGradientAlongPathPerS2.note: Scalar magnitude gradient only. Direction rotation is tracked separately.

tidalGradientAlongPathPerMS2.note: Finite-difference change in tidal Frobenius norm along the route segment.

accelerationDirectionChangeRad.note: A changing acceleration direction can mark saddle or multi-source geometry even when scalar acceleration is modest.

mathematicalRules: Route safety is C_route = AND_i C_segment,i. One blocking interval rejects the route regardless of the number of benign intervals.
Segment length is Delta s_i = (f_{i+1}-f_i)L for route fraction f and route chord length L.
A sampled segment envelope is a numerical bound only over its sampled endpoints unless adaptive refinement or analytic analysis supplies stronger evidence.
Potential, acceleration, tidal loading and curvature retain their native dimensions through the physical layer and are normalized only by the versioned physical-to-family bridge.
Finite-difference gradients are convergence diagnostics and hazard-localization aids; they are not exact spatial derivatives without an appropriate limiting/convergence argument.
canonSafeguards: This registry does not establish that FTL is physically realizable.
This registry does not assign an FTL family to any race, civilization, vessel or manufacturer.
Ordinary gravitational segmentation constrains fictional transit models but does not invent family-boundary hazards.
A blocked physical segment may not be erased by averaging it with benign route segments.
PARTIAL, UNRESOLVED and OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY remain visible evidence states and may not be converted into ordinary finite safe scores.
Segment thresholds or numerical margins introduced by downstream calibration remain DERIVED or PROPOSED unless a higher authority establishes them.
